html:
Carlos Antonio López was the ruler of Paraguay from 1841 until his death in 1862, first as consul and then as president. He opened the country that Francia had closed.

He made peace with neighbours, won recognition of independence, and invited European engineers. They built an ironworks, a shipyard, a telegraph and one of the first railways in South America. He sent his son, Francisco Solano López, to Europe to buy arms and hire experts, and built a strong army and river fortress at Humaitá.

He also kept a tight hand: there was no free press, and the state held most land and trade, run for his family's benefit. When he died, his son inherited a modern army and a country ready to fight, which it soon did in the War of the Triple Alliance that ruined Paraguay.
sum: Carlos Antonio López was the ruler of Paraguay from 1841 until his death in 1862, first as consul and then as president. He opened the country that Francia had closed.
